title: Terahertz Atom Probe Tomography
content: The use of ultrashort phenomena to trigger the field evaporation of the ion is mandatory in atomic probe tomography to perform time-of-flight mass spectrometry. Today, either laser or electric pulses are used depending on the material being analyzed, but their disadvantages are well known: laser pulses heat up the sample [1], while electric pulses produce ions with a large energy spread [2]. In both cases, large bias is observed in the measurement of composition. In this talk, we propose a newly developed instrument that uses a high-amplitude terahertz (THz) monocycle to trigger field evaporation. We will present the configuration based on two-color filamentation in air coupled with a custom APT, as shown in Figure 1. First results on metals show that there is neither ions energy spread nor sample temperature increase. The THz monocycle acts as an ultra-short electrical pulse [3-5].
